questions.title: Build and Print a Color Palette
questions.description:
You are helping a design tool store its color palette. Read n color names, build a list by appending each name in order, then show the finished palette.

Input Format:
First line: integer n. Next n lines: one color name per line (a single word).

Output Format:
Line 1: the list exactly as Python prints it. Line 2: the number of colors in the list.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20; color names are single words of up to 15 letters.
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 20, one color word per line
questions.sourcecode:
n = int(input())
colors = []
for _ in range(n):
    colors.append(input())
print(colors)
print(len(colors))

questions.title: Insert Append Remove Drill
questions.description:
A warm-up drill on the core list methods. Start with four integers, then apply three operations in order: insert a value at a position, append a value, and remove the first occurrence of a value.

Input Format:
Line 1: four integers separated by spaces. Line 2: x and pos — insert integer x at 0-based position pos. Line 3: integer y to append. Line 4: integer z, guaranteed to be present in the list at that moment; remove its first occurrence.

Output Format:
The final list, exactly as Python prints it.

Constraints:
List values are integers in -1000..1000; 0 <= pos <= current list length; z is always present when its removal runs.
questions.inputconstrains: four initial integers, then x pos, then y, then z; values in -1000..1000
questions.sourcecode:
nums = list(map(int, input().split()))
x, pos = map(int, input().split())
y = int(input())
z = int(input())
nums.insert(pos, x)
nums.append(y)
nums.remove(z)
print(nums)

questions.title: Score Index and Count
questions.description:
Six quiz scores are recorded in a list. Report where a target score first appears and how many times it appears overall, using the list methods index and count.

Input Format:
Line 1: six integers separated by spaces. Line 2: the target integer, guaranteed to be present in the list.

Output Format:
Line 1: the index of the first occurrence of the target. Line 2: the number of occurrences of the target.

Constraints:
Exactly 6 integers per list, each in -100..100; the target is guaranteed to appear at least once.
questions.inputconstrains: exactly 6 integers in -100..100; target guaranteed present
questions.sourcecode:
scores = list(map(int, input().split()))
target = int(input())
print(scores.index(target))
print(scores.count(target))

questions.title: Slice Three Ways
questions.description:
Take one list of integers and practice three kinds of slicing: the first three elements, the last three elements, and every second element starting at index 0.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n (at least 6). Line 2: n integers separated by spaces.

Output Format:
Line 1: the first three elements as a list. Line 2: the last three elements as a list. Line 3: every second element (step 2) as a list. All three lines use Python's list printing format.

Constraints:
6 <= n <= 100; values in -1000..1000.
questions.sourcecode:
n = int(input())
vals = list(map(int, input().split()))
print(vals[:3])
print(vals[-3:])
print(vals[::2])

questions.title: Swap Two Values with Tuple Unpacking
questions.description:
Python lets two variables exchange values in one statement thanks to tuple packing and unpacking. Read two integers, swap them using the statement a, b = b, a, and print the result.

Input Format:
One line with two integers separated by a space.

Output Format:
One line with the two integers after the swap, separated by a space (first the swapped a, then the swapped b).

Constraints:
Both integers are in -1000000..1000000.
questions.inputconstrains: two integers in -1000000..1000000
questions.sourcecode:
a, b = map(int, input().split())
a, b = b, a
print(a, b)

questions.title: Tuple Snapshot Basics
questions.description:
Capture a set of words as an immutable tuple, then inspect it: the whole tuple, its first element, its last element, and its length.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: one word per line.

Output Format:
Line 1: the tuple exactly as Python prints it. Line 2: the first element. Line 3: the last element. Line 4: the number of elements in the tuple.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20; words are single tokens of up to 15 characters.
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 20, one word per line
questions.sourcecode:
n = int(input())
words = []
for _ in range(n):
    words.append(input())
record = tuple(words)
print(record)
print(record[0])
print(record[-1])
print(len(record))

questions.title: Checkout Cart Total
questions.description:
A cashier scans items at a grocery register, recording each price into the cart list. After all items are scanned, the register reports how many items were bought and the total amount due.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n, the number of scanned items. Next n lines: one price per line, a decimal amount with at most 2 decimal places.

Output Format:
Line 1: the number of items in the cart. Line 2: the total of all prices, formatted to exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50; each price satisfies 0 <= price <= 1000 and has at most 2 decimal places.
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 50, 0 <= price <= 1000 with at most 2 decimals
questions.sourcecode:
n = int(input())
cart = []
for _ in range(n):
    cart.append(float(input()))
total = 0.0
for price in cart:
    total += price
print(len(cart))
print(f"{total:.2f}")

questions.title: Road Trip Playlist Manager
questions.description:
Before a long drive you curate a road-trip playlist. Start with n songs, then insert one new song at a given position, then drop one song you are tired of by name. Show the final playlist.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: one song name per line (a single word). Next line: pos and song — insert song at 0-based position pos. Last line: a song name that is guaranteed to be in the playlist; remove it.

Output Format:
The final playlist, one song per line, in order.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 20; song names are single words of up to 20 characters; pos is a valid position.
questions.input1:
4
aria
bolt
chime
drift
2 echo
bolt
questions.inputconstrains: 2 <= n <= 20; pos valid; removed song guaranteed present
questions.sourcecode:
n = int(input())
playlist = []
for _ in range(n):
    playlist.append(input())
pos, song = input().split()
playlist.insert(int(pos), song)
gone = input()
playlist.remove(gone)
for track in playlist:
    print(track)

questions.title: Greenhouse Temperature Log
questions.description:
A greenhouse logs one temperature reading per day for a week (7 readings). The keeper wants to review the start of the week, the end of the week, and the average of the final three days.

Input Format:
One line with exactly 7 integers separated by spaces (the daily readings).

Output Format:
Line 1: the first three readings as a list. Line 2: the last three readings as a list. Line 3: the average of the last three readings, formatted to exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
Exactly 7 integers, each in -50..60.
questions.inputconstrains: exactly 7 integers in -50..60
questions.sourcecode:
readings = list(map(int, input().split()))
print(readings[:3])
tail = readings[-3:]
print(tail)
avg = (tail[0] + tail[1] + tail[2]) / 3
print(f"{avg:.2f}")

questions.title: Server Log Tail

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: the log lines (they may contain spaces). Last line: integer k.

Output Format:
The last k log lines, one per line, in original order.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= n <= 100; each log line is non-empty and up to 60 characters.

questions.title: Grocery Checkout with Corrections
questions.description:
A grocery cart holds item prices (whole dollars) in scan order. Before payment the cashier applies corrections: POP pos removes the item at 0-based position pos; RM value removes the first occurrence of that exact price. After all corrections, compute the amount due.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Line 2: n integer prices separated by spaces. Line 3: integer m, the number of corrections. Next m lines: one correction each, either "POP pos" or "RM value".

Output Format:
One integer: the total of the remaining prices.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; 0 <= m <= n; prices in 1..500; every correction is valid (pos in range, value present when RM runs). Do not use the built-in sum() — practice a manual accumulation loop, and use pop/remove for the corrections.
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= m <= n, prices in 1..500, corrections always valid

questions.title: Rotate the Duty Roster
questions.description:
A team lead rotates the weekly duty roster to the right by k positions: everyone shifts k places forward and the last k people wrap around to the front. Achieve the rotation with list slicing only — no loops that move elements one by one, no reversal helpers.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: one name per line (a single word). Last line: integer k.

Output Format:
One line with the rotated names separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 100; 1 <= k < n; names are single words of up to 20 characters.
questions.input2:
6
p1
p2
p3
p4
p5
p6
3
questions.output2: p4 p5 p6 p1 p2 p3
questions.sourcecode:
n = int(input())
lst = [input() for _ in range(n)]
k = int(input())
rotated = lst[-k:] + lst[:-k]
print(" ".join(rotated))

questions.title: Sort Stall Prices by Hand
questions.description:
A market stall keeper wants their price board sorted from cheapest to most expensive, but the cash terminal is broken — no built-in sorting allowed. Implement selection sort by hand: repeatedly find the smallest remaining price and swap it into place, sorting the list in place.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Line 2: n integer prices separated by spaces.

Output Format:
One line with the prices in ascending order, separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; prices in 1..1000.

questions.title: Sliding Window Peak Load
questions.description:
A data center records one load sample per minute. Given the samples and a window width w, slide a window of size w across the samples from left to right and report the peak (highest value) inside each window. Find each peak with a manual scan — no max() or min().

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Line 2: n integer readings separated by spaces. Line 3: integer w.

Output Format:
One line with the n - w + 1 window peaks separated by single spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= w <= n <= 500; readings in 0..1000.
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= w <= n <= 500, readings in 0..1000
questions.sourcecode:
n = int(input())
readings = list(map(int, input().split()))
w = int(input())
peaks = []
for i in range(n - w + 1):
    best = readings[i]
    for j in range(i, i + w):
        if readings[j] > best:
            best = readings[j]
    peaks.append(best)
print(" ".join(map(str, peaks)))

questions.title: Workshop Badge Records
questions.description:
A workshop checks in attendees and packs each record as an immutable tuple: (name, score, status), where status is pass when the score is at least 50 and fail otherwise. After all records are packed, unpack each tuple in a loop to print the badge sheet.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: name and score separated by a space (score is an integer).

Output Format:
One line per attendee: name, score, and status separated by single spaces, in input order.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50; names are single words; scores in 0..100.
questions.sampleoutput1:
ana 82 pass
bob 41 fail
cal 50 pass
questions.output2:
gus 60 pass
hana 59 pass
ivan 58 pass
juno 57 pass
questions.output3:
kim 50 pass
lee 50 pass
mara 51 pass
questions.sourcecode:
n = int(input())
records = []
for _ in range(n):
    name, score = input().split()
    score = int(score)
    status = "pass" if score >= 50 else "fail"
    records.append(tuple([name, score, status]))
for name, score, status in records:
    print(name, score, status)

questions.title: Immutable Audit Trail
questions.description:
A security appliance appends events to an audit trail that must stay immutable, so the trail is modeled as a tuple that grows only by concatenation — never by list mutation methods. Read the events, build the tuple trail, then report its size and the most recent event.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: an event per line, formatted as code followed by a message (the message may contain spaces).

Output Format:
Line 1: the number of events in the trail. Line 2: the most recent event as "code message".

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50; each line is at most 80 characters; the code is a single token and the message is non-empty.
questions.sampleinput1:
3
E100 system boot
E205 disk retry
E310 backup done
questions.input1:
2
W010 low memory
W020 high latency
questions.input2:
4
A1 one
A2 two words
A3 three word line
A4 end
questions.input3:
2
X9 final event here
Y8 newer
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 50, event lines up to 80 chars
questions.sourcecode:
n = int(input())
log = ()
for _ in range(n):
    code, message = input().split(" ", 1)
    log = log + ((code, message),)
print(len(log))
last_code, last_message = log[-1]
print(last_code, last_message)

questions.title: Warehouse Pallet Allocation
questions.description:
A warehouse loads arriving pallets onto trucks using a first-fit rule. Each truck has a capacity; pallets arrive in a fixed order. Every pallet is placed onto the FIRST truck (in input order) whose remaining capacity can hold it; if no truck can take it, the pallet stays on the dock. Trucks keep pallets in the order they were loaded.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer t, the number of trucks. Line 2: t integer capacities separated by spaces. Line 3: integer n, the number of pallets. Line 4: n integer weights separated by spaces (arrival order).

Output Format:
One line per truck, in input order: "Truck i: w1 w2 ... | left: r" where the w's are the pallet weights loaded on that truck in loading order and r is the remaining capacity. If a truck loaded nothing, print "Truck i: | left: r". Final line: "Dock: w1 w2 ..." with the unloaded pallets in arrival order, or "Dock:" if the dock is empty.

Constraints:
1 <= t <= 10; 1 <= n <= 100; capacities and weights in 1..1000. No sorting is needed or allowed — process everything in input order and accumulate totals manually (no sum()).
questions.output2:
Truck 1: | left: 5
Truck 2: | left: 5
Truck 3: | left: 5
Dock: 6 7
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= t <= 10, 1 <= n <= 100, capacities and weights in 1..1000

questions.title: Exam Seat Reallocation
questions.description:
An exam hall keeps its seating chart as an ordered list of student names. The invigilator applies a batch of reallocation operations: JOIN pos name seats a student at 0-based position pos; LEAVE pos removes whoever sits at position pos; MOVE a b removes the student at position a and re-seats them at position b of the list that results from that removal; SWAP p q exchanges the students at positions p and q. Names may repeat, so every operation works on positions, not names.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: the initial seating, one name per line. Line n+2: integer m, the number of operations. Next m lines: one operation each (JOIN pos name / LEAVE pos / MOVE a b / SWAP p q).

Output Format:
The final seating chart, one name per line.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50; 0 <= m <= 50; names are single words of up to 20 characters; all positions are guaranteed valid (JOIN pos satisfies 0 <= pos <= current length; for MOVE, b is valid in the list after the removal). Use pop/insert based list surgery; do not use remove(), del, or any sorting.

questions.title: Tuple Ledger Reconciliation
questions.description:
A tiny accounting app stores ledgers as immutable tuples of (key, value) pairs. Ledger A and ledger B must be reconciled into ONE tuple ledger: start from A's entries in order, then process B's entries in order — if a key is already present, that entry's value is replaced in place; otherwise the new entry is appended at the end. Because tuples are immutable, every replacement and append must rebuild the tuple via concatenation (no dicts, no lists of records, no mutation).

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: key and integer value separated by a space (ledger A, keys unique within A). Next line: integer m. Next m lines: key and integer value (ledger B, keys unique within B).

Output Format:
The reconciled ledger, one "key value" pair per line, in merged order.

Constraints:
1 <= n, m <= 50; keys are single tokens of up to 15 characters; values in 0..1000; keys are unique within each ledger (they may overlap between ledgers).
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n, m <= 50, values in 0..1000, keys unique per ledger
questions.sourcecode:
n = int(input())
ledger = ()
keys = ()
for _ in range(n):
    k, v = input().split()
    ledger = ledger + ((k, int(v)),)
    keys = keys + (k,)
m = int(input())
for _ in range(m):
    k, v = input().split()
    v = int(v)
    if k in keys:
        i = keys.index(k)
        ledger = ledger[:i] + ((k, v),) + ledger[i + 1:]
    else:
        ledger = ledger + ((k, v),)
        keys = keys + (k,)
for k, v in ledger:
    print(k, v)

questions.title: Round Robin Tournament Scheduler
questions.description:
A chess club schedules a round-robin tournament for an even number of players using the circle method: the player at index 0 stays fixed, and in every round each player is paired against the player mirroring them in the list (position i versus position n-1-i). After each round, everyone except the fixed player rotates one step: the list becomes [first] + [last] + everything between them. Print all n-1 rounds.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n (even). Next n lines: one player name per line (unique, single words).

Output Format:
All pairings, one per line as "a vs b", in round order and within each round from the ends toward the middle.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 10 with n even; names are single words of up to 20 characters. Pure slicing rotation — no itertools, no deque, no reversal helpers.
